usageNotes: Suspends a running QEMU VM, either to RAM (default, VM remains in memory and resumes instantly) or to disk via todisk=true (state written to storage, VM fully powers off and resumes on next start). Returns an async task UPID — poll the task status endpoint to confirm completion before assuming the VM is suspended. Suspending to disk requires additional privileges (VM.Config.Disk on the VM and Datastore.AllocateSpace on the target storage); if statestorage is omitted, Proxmox selects the default storage, which must support VM state snapshots.

examples.summary: Suspend VM 105 to disk on node pve1, storing state on local-lvm

destructiveReason: Suspending to RAM pauses all VM CPU/IO activity (service interruption); suspending to disk fully powers down the VM, making its services unavailable until it is manually started again.
tips: RAM suspend (todisk omitted or false) keeps VM memory allocated on the node — do not migrate or stop the node while VMs are in RAM-suspend state or their state will be lost.
Use todisk=true for long-term hibernation or maintenance windows where the node itself may be rebooted.
The returned UPID string can be passed to GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to monitor suspend progress.
skiplock is root-only; avoid using it unless a stuck lock is confirmed — forcibly skipping a lock on an actively-used VM risks data corruption.
